title: Vesper Reach — The Cost of a Counter
provisional_story: Three separate combat-sequence studies in the same provisional world; no automatic chronology, owner-selected cast or canon. Duel12, squad6, siege6.

budget.per_image: One primary; at most one R1 structural correction for an observed hard failure and one F1 source-only surface redraw for observed competing texture. Inspect contacts before finishing. No beauty loops or allowance padding. A failed service call may be retried unchanged at most once, with at most two such retry calls in the whole round; all calls count toward56. A single documented no-art input-validation resubmission may instead remove one redundant sixth reference to satisfy the built-in five-reference limit; preserve the failed request, keep the creative brief unchanged, and debit the existing retry and total invocation caps. This is not a structural repair or extra primary image.

acceptance.action: Every exchange needs setup, real force/contact, counter or consequence; no generic posed glow. Read continuous sequences without explanatory captions before claiming causality.
acceptance.continuity: Carry mantle notch, left sleeve abrasion and wall patch within duel; shield chip, ice wedge and broken horn within squad; falling/missing bridge and ice route within siege. Studies are not one timeline.
acceptance.texture: Preserve approved drawing and quiet broad materials; source-only redraw when needed, never silently fix anatomy by surface claims.
acceptance.preference: New choices blank, owner feedback global direction only. Technical and AI review are not owner approval.

No violet wall, no rising force ramp, one thin floor boundary and severe physical strain. The bridge loss must be unmistakable and irreversible.

power.description: A planted Axis Lance turns the direction of weight inside one narrow ground strip.
power.limitation: The butt must remain planted, the caster within reach and outside the strip; every loose body and water inside follows the same direction.
power.growth: Turn a wider burden or collapsing structure at great strain; force direction must remain intelligible.

entries.title: What victory leaves behind
entries.caption: They saved the column and sacrificed the main road.
entries.brief: Independent siege test, not chronological after duel or squad. WEST/LEFT is a monumental open retreat gate and safe bank. EAST/RIGHT has the attacking army and an immense four-legged armored organic siege beast with one brass mouth collar. A broad bridge runs left/right over a deep canal. A parallel lower canal edge provides the alternate ice retreat route. Three recurring defenders: Neris, Kellan, Ilyra; no Riven in this test. Organized adult military ranks and a retreating adult column; no child figures. Pale dawn and restrained ochre banners distinguish this battlefield from the duel. Extreme-wide aftermath in warmer dawn. LEFT safe bank holds an organized exhausted adult column passing inside the monumental gate as it closes behind them, three tiny recognizable heroes at its edge: Neris leaning on crescent, Kellan lifting broad sword from water after the crossing, Ilyra kneeling beside upright lance. RIGHT attacking masses and lowered four-legged siege beast remain separated by a visibly MISSING main bridge center span, broad fallen slabs in the canal. The parallel ice route remains visible but is guarded at its safe end, with its working edge no longer growing after blade lift. Breaking the main span delayed heavy pursuit and bought retreat time; do not imply this alone prevents every enemy from taking the ice route. Big territory/scale/cost shapes, few purposeful faces in nearest survivors, quiet water and light. Do not restore the bridge, erase the enemy or end on a giant hero portrait.
